Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.
Heard counsel for the applicant and Sri Madan Singh, counsel for the informant and Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned AGA for the State.
Perused the material on record.
2. The applicant was granted interim anticipatory bail vide order dated 17.9.2024 by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court.
The order is quoted herein below;-
"1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned AGA and perused the material available on record.

2. The present Anticipatory Bail Application has been filed with the prayer to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant - Narendra Singh in Case Crime No. 45 of 2020 Narendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148844725/

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant was the Principal of the Intermediate college duly selected by the U.P. Secondary Education Service Selection Board.

entities.text: U.P. Secondary Education Service Selection Board
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that at present applicant had resigned and after resignation the informant who was having rivalry has lodged First Information Report after six years of selection.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in the First Information Report there are allegations that the fake mark-sheets were produced before the Selection Board.
Neither the Selection Board has held any enquiry with regard to the document produced by the applicant nor Board has given any report with regard to the fact that documents were fake in nature.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the investigation in the present case has been proceeded only on the basis of oral statement of the witnesses.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that once documents which have been issued by the government authority is in dispute, it was necessary for the Investigating Officer to have sent the same to the Board of High School and other Board which have issued the mark sheets for verification and only on the basis of oral statement of the witnesses, the same cannot be construed that the mark sheets are fake.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has no concern with the present matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
No prima facie case is made out against the applicant.
If the applicant is enlarged on anticipatory bail, he will not misuse the liberty and cooperate with the investigation.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest by the police any time.
4. Learned A.G.A. for the State is directed to file counter affidavit bringing on record the evidence found during investigation against the applicant.
Learned A.G.A. for the State shall also disclose whether the disputed marksheets were sent to the respective Boards from where the same were issued for verification.

5. List this case on 16.10.2024 in top ten cases.
6.
As an interim protection, till the next date fixed for final hearing on this application, the applicant is granted interim anticipatory bail in the aforesaid case crime number.

In the event of arrest of the applicant, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the court concerned and participate in the trial court proceedings.

entities.text: Narendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office.
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court concerned.

(iv) In the event, the applicant changes residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned/Investigating Officer about new residential address in writing.
7.
In case of default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of interim protection granted to the applicant."
3. Counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant has furnished bail bonds in terms of the interim order dated 17.9.2024 passed by this Court.
The applicant is appearing before the concerned court on the dates fixed.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
In case, the applicant is released on anticipatory bail, till the conclusion of trial he will not misuse the said liberty.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.

5. Having regard to the submissions made by counsel for the applicant as recorded in the order dated 17.9.2024, considering the nature of accusations, antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is appearing before the concerned court on the dates fixed.

Further, no violation of conditions or misuse of liberty of interim anticipatory bail has been pointed out by learned AGA, without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
